sourceInformation.source: Advanced Dungeons & Dragons (Intellivision, 1982), later subtitled Cloudy Mountain
sourceInformation.tech: JavaScript, HTML/CSS; unmodified my-3D2dge v0.89.1 (commit 8ecc2f62353761187bdfe226f327b7ea5d2eb691), unmodified AI Hub session client v1.4.0 / Session Protocol v1 (commit 35a1047f2067b2af3de3943f0fe452f39105d869); Web Audio and WebRTC; no runtime asset dependencies
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original shaded pixel and skeletal native-engine art, miniature wilderness, pale stone/root/cistern/amber/blue cave palettes
sourceInformation.animation: Native Humanoid poses, weapon and hand attachments; original articulated creature rigs driven by authoritative simulation state
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-synthesized music, effects, ambience and formant-gibberish voices; music 10% by default; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 players: solo, couch co-op, manual-signaling direct WebRTC, AI Hub shared-world sessions with dedicated-server support. Two-context local/file and adverse Hub tests passed. Physical devices and WAN/NAT reachability: unknown.
sourceInformation.testing: Automated headless testing was permitted without a rendering performance budget. Checked the standard-rule full expedition, Chromium/WebKit, emulated DualSense and multitouch, measured Web Audio, real two-copy WebRTC and six unchanged Hub harness cases. Exact counts and reports are in docs/verification.md. Real controller/iPhone/TV, human listening and WAN/NAT reachability: unknown. First-player 18–25-minute pacing is unmeasured.
sourceInformation.research: Read Blue Sky Rangers original instructions and production history; inspected the original map/cave screenshot. Embedded gameplay video and original audio: unknown. Read pinned engine handoff/API/assets/adventure/roguelike and full Hub contract/client/harness; checked primary W3C/WebRTC peer-connection documentation.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux Ubuntu 26.04.1 under WSL2

testingFeedback: Eight distinct defects were found and fixed: stale revival input, invalid saved actor coordinates, denied storage access at construction, title action overflow, touch HUD interception, ignored miniature palette options, checkpoint roster restoration and an asynchronous snapshot crossing a reconnection. Test-driver mistakes and repeated assertions are not counted.

Three defects were potentially game breaking: denied storage could stop startup, an invalid actor save could break resume, and an old checkpoint could restore a departed companion who then blocked progression. A separate high-severity reconnection snapshot race affected guest views. All have regression coverage.

The legitimate production-command full-expedition director was most helpful: it exercised ammunition, navigation, guardian windows, all tools, both relic halves, death recovery and final resolution without cheats.

The first stopped-clock guardian screenshots were least helpful: game.advance requires draw:true in a browser, so those initial captures showed an old frame. They were replaced with explicit rendered fixtures.
engineFeedback: Native Humanoid hand attachments, shaded primitives, materials, depth queues and the built-in Shell made a consistent visual and controller interface possible without asset files.
I initially assumed browser game.advance drew a frame by default and passed color where terrain helpers require base/dark/light. Reading the precise contracts and visual checks corrected both.
The authoritative expedition simulation: swept recoverable ricochets, passage-based hearing, visibility memory, shared resource/checkpoint rules and transport adapters.
Keeping world units, native attachment coordinates, camera framing, fog overlays and visible-threat omission consistent across local, dedicated-server and remote copies.
None. The full pinned engine is unmodified; bow poses, creatures, hearing, campaign, touch adaptation and networking are game extensions.
A documented native bow kit linking hand attachments, draw/release timing and swept projectile collision would be useful.
promptFeedback: The concrete mechanics, tool chain, native-art direction, exact delivery names and evidence requirements made the intended expedition clear.

The brief calls the result a demo while PLAN.md calls for a complete 18–25-minute authored expedition; I treated the plan as the scope. Physical first-play pacing cannot be established by a headless expert replay.
Integrating scarce-arrow exploration, recoverable banks, acoustic information, restart solvability, three input families and two production network transports into one coherent campaign.
Separate functional acceptance from first-player pacing evaluation, and provide a small official shared-world/bow integration fixture alongside the engine handoff.

aiHub.name: Advanced Dungeons & Near Misses
aiHub.tagline: A little nerve. Three good arrows.
aiHub.description: Two dragons keep the daylight. Listen through stone, bank and reclaim your arrows, and carry the axe, boat and key toward the broken Crown of Clear Skies. Explore 29 authored chambers alone or with a fellow ranger.
aiHub.controls: WASD / left stick move; mouse / right stick aim; click / R2 fire; right click / L2 listen; E / Cross interact; Space / Circle quickstep; Tab / Triangle map; touch zones supported.
